claims.statement: GET /api/v1/access (admin) is a read-only projection {schema_version: 1, principals, roles, policy} whose policy.configured matches /meta authorization.namespace_policy.
Under a namespace policy an observation receipt omits the store revision, reporting it absent as policy_scoped.
Without a bearer, POST /observations gets the constant 401 ACCESS.authorization_denied block (category permission, param null, message Forbidden) and GET /access gets 401 with the common error body.
POST /behavioral/events requires a source id in context (422 without it) and returns an empty list when no directive matches.
The causal engine never mutates the store: intervene, counterfactual and propagate leave vectors and the store revision unchanged.

expect.why: causal calls committed no store transaction

claims.statement: Graph-free and missing-record causal routes: validate-dag answers {valid: true, message: null} or 400 on a cycle, mechanisms include linear, additive_noise and polynomial, intervene and subgraph answer 404 for a missing record, and causal/resolve answers empty results for a missing source.
do(X=value) returns {variable_id, value, affected_ids, trace} and affected_ids include the causal descendants of X.
POST /causal/counterfactual returns factual, counterfactual and diff, where diff maps each changed variable to its numeric difference (e.g. "var-b": -1.0).
POST /causal/resolve returns only XTypes reachable via CAUSAL-type vectors.
kairos-observe mints a UUIDv7 idempotency key, prints it on stderr, and rerunning with --idempotency-key KEY replays instead of re-applying.

GET /api/v1/health returns only {status, version, timestamp} (also at the /health alias), /api/v1/health/ready answers 200 with ready true and a components object on a started node, and all three are exempt from rate limiting (no X-RateLimit-* headers).

Every response, including errors, carries the documented security headers with the documented values (HSTS max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, CSP default-src 'none', nosniff, DENY, no-store, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, empty permissions policy).
Rate-limited responses carry X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset (100 for reads, 30 for writes), and every response carries X-Request-ID, echoing a client-supplied value or a fresh UUID v4.
A request body over 1 MB is rejected with 413 and error.type PayloadTooLargeError before any route runs.
All error responses share the structured body {"error": {"type", "message", "detail"}}.
/docs, /redoc and /openapi.json return 404 unless KAIROS_DEBUG=true.
GET /metrics is exempt from rate limiting (no X-RateLimit-* headers).

With auth on, /api/v1/meta, /api/v1/health and /api/v1/health/ready answer without a token, while a data route without a bearer gets 401 {"error": {"type": "AuthenticationError", "message": "Authentication required", "detail": null}}.
GET /metrics is exempt from authentication (answers without a bearer token).
An observation applies one ema-phi-v1 step (w <- 0.618*w + 0.382*signal), answers 201 with outcome applied, and the stored weight equals the receipt weight.
An ema-phi-v1 result below 0.382 collapses to 0.
Because an adaptive edge is admitted only at or above 0.618, one observation can open a route (0.5 -> 0.65) or close one (0.7 -> 0.55).
A retry with the same idempotency key and payload replays: 201, outcome replayed, the stored receipt, and no second learning step.
The same key with a different payload is refused with 409 OBSERVATION.idempotency_key_conflict (not retryable) and applies nothing.
REST, the agent tool observe and MCP kairos_observe share one key space: a retry on another surface replays.
Without a namespace policy an observation receipt carries the store revision {instance_id, recorded_seq}, and a replay returns the same revision.
recorded_seq advances by exactly 1 per committed transaction that changes XType or vector rows, and a replay does not move it.

expect.why: one write since obs-a (replay moves nothing); assumes no concurrent writers

claims.statement: Public reads never change weights: resolves, queries and MCP/agent-tool reads leave adaptive weights, vector versions and the store revision untouched.

Observation bodies are validated: a missing key is 422 idempotency_key_required, a body carrying update is 422 observation_update_retired, and a signal outside [0, 1], a boolean or string signal, an unknown field or both selectors are 422 invalid_input; nothing is applied.

Edge selection refusals: unknown vector_id or an unjoined pair is 404 observation_edge_not_found, an unknown endpoint is 400 observation_endpoint_not_found, a non-adaptive vector is 422 observation_edge_not_adaptive, and a pair joined by two adaptive vectors is 422 observation_edge_ambiguous.

GET /api/v1/observations (admin) lists receipts newest first as {schema_version: 1, items, page: {next_cursor, partial}}, with writer absent as not_stored, and refuses limit outside 1..100 with 422 OBSERVATION.invalid_input naming limit.
There is no read API for observation history: no per-observation or history route exists beyond the 24-hour admin receipt list.
MCP initialize answers protocolVersion 2025-11-25 with serverInfo {name: kairos, version: <node version>}, and notifications/initialized answers HTTP 202.

MCP tools/list exposes exactly 9 tools (kairos_resolve, kairos_observe and seven kairos_federation_* tools), each with an inputSchema; only kairos_observe and kairos_resolve also declare an outputSchema.
GET /mcp returns 405 (no SSE stream), another MCP-Protocol-Version header gets HTTP 400, and a request carrying an Origin header is refused with 403 when no origin is allowed.
JSON-RPC errors are HTTP 200: malformed JSON is -32700, an unknown method or unknown tool name is -32601.
kairos_observe without idempotency_key is an isError tool result carrying OBSERVATION.idempotency_key_required, not a JSON-RPC error.

kairos_resolve ranks a source's admitted edges in the same order as POST /api/v1/resolve and returns a CallToolResult whose structuredContent is the result envelope and whose content[0].text is the same JSON.
The federation tools identity, capabilities and health are not gated: they answer without a bearer token.
Every POST /mcp counts against a write limit of 30 requests per minute per client; past it the node answers 429 with Retry-After.

expect.why: a burst of pings must hit 429 within 31 requests

claims.statement: GET /api/v1/meta is auth-exempt, answers 200 application/json with Cache-Control: no-store, accepts HEAD, refuses other methods, and reports the same version as /health.
With authentication off, /meta reports auth.enabled false, auth.provider and auth.privy_app_id null, and mcp.requires_bearer equal to auth.enabled.
On the PostgreSQL profile /meta reports Privy auth on (provider privy, a public app id), admin_waiver false, mcp.requires_bearer true and store.backend postgres.
/meta.mcp describes the pinned transport (path /mcp, protocol 2025-11-25, streamable-http, JSON responses, no sessions) and lists the MCP tools in tools/list order.
/meta.agent_tools lists the seven documented agent tools, and every write (W) tool carries idempotency_key: required.
/meta never carries an env id, hostname, namespace, peer URLs, Origin allowlist entries, keys or secrets.

expect.why: federation env_id must not leak through /meta

claims.statement: PRODUCT.md states auth mode is not discoverable and no /meta route exists (GET /api/v1/meta would be 404).
A structural vector is always admitted, whatever the request context.
A contextual vector is admitted only when every one of its parameters matches the context.
Parameter matching is exact or any-of: a list parameter admits a context value (or any context list member) that is in the list.
A causal vector is admitted only when its parameters match the context (and it is not blocked by an intervention).
The public resolve context accepts only user, roles, locale and timestamp (extra: forbid); interventions cannot be smuggled in through it.
An adaptive vector is admitted only while its learned weight is at least 0.618.
An adaptive edge is admitted at or above 0.618, so an edge whose weight is exactly 0.618 is admitted.
Behavioral edges resolve only through the behavioral event path, never from a public resolve (REST or MCP).
service_chain vectors can be created but never resolve, because no resolver is registered.
Admitted targets are ranked by weight, highest first.
Resolution is deterministic: the same graph and context give the same answer, and the resolve agent tool returns the same order as POST /resolve.
The documented POST /resolve request example ({"locale": "en", "role": "admin"} context) is a valid request.
An empty context ({}) resolves only structural vectors.
With roles containing "prefer-declared", targets whose metadata.accessor equals another requested role rank by weight x 1.618; without it the order is the weight order; stored weights never change.
There are no time windows: the context timestamp never changes which vectors are admitted.
Compositional traversal: chain refuses more than 8 steps with 422, and reachable returns a depth map of readable targets that excludes the source.
The resolve response field trace is the resolution trace log (published OpenAPI description "Resolution trace log"): a resolution that admits targets records its steps there.

expect.why: a trace log of a non-empty resolution is not empty

claims.statement: GET /resolve?query= is a text search returning {results, query, threshold} with threshold defaulting to 0.5.
Idempotency keys are stored as SHA-256 only: the key row holds sha256(key) and the raw key appears in no stored column.

claims.statement: A key whose stored row is older than 24 hours never replays: the retry is refused with 409 OBSERVATION.idempotency_key_expired, nothing is applied, and GET /observations no longer lists it.

sqlite.sql: UPDATE idempotency_keys SET created_at = ? WHERE key_hash = ?

claims.statement: A write tool without idempotency_key is an HTTP 200 envelope with outcome rejected, data null, error.code XTYPE.idempotency_key_required (param idempotency_key) and a null operation key.
Agent-tool creates are retry-safe: the same key and input replay (outcome replayed, same id, nothing written twice); the same key with other input is XTYPE.idempotency_key_conflict.
execute-batch runs every tool regardless of failures and reports all_success false when any result has an error.
An unknown tool name, including reload_seed, is refused with TOOL.unknown_tool (param tool) before any handler runs.
Vector endpoints must reference existing XTypes: POST /vectors with an unknown source is 400, and GET /vectors/from|to/{unknown} is 400.
A vector weight below 0.382 collapses to 0.0 and a weight above 1.0 clamps to 1.0.
vector_type must be one of contextual, structural, causal, behavioral, adaptive; any other value is refused with 422.

expect.why: service_chain is not in the documented enumeration

claims.statement: POST /xtypes creates at version 1 (201) with the documented fields, a duplicate id is 409, GET /xtypes/fqn/{namespace.name} finds it (404 when absent), and PATCH increments the version (sent with the store's expected_version token; see KC-XTYPE-006).
XType validation: kind outside data|model|service|vector_def|directive, a model without a name, a namespace deeper than 5 levels, and unknown GET /xtypes query parameters are refused with 422.
DELETE /xtypes/{id} deletes the XType and cascade-deletes its vectors (sent with the store's expected_version token; see KC-XTYPE-006).
Creating an XType whose id starts with kairos.access: outside the kairos.access namespace is refused with 403 "XType ids and names under 'kairos.access' are reserved for that namespace".
